subject: Inference enclave qualification — post-call recap
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novamed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-09T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inference enclave qualification — post-call recap

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick written recap so we have the same reference and clear next steps. I captured the items we discussed about your inference requirements and the path toward a committed environment. If I missed anything, please flag.

Key pain points you described:
- Unpredictable latency under peak traffic (p99 spikes ~600–800ms) impacting UX for clinician workflows.
- Concern about data residency and multi-tenant noise (you cannot tolerate co-located models on the same GPU hosts).
- Cost variability during weekly batch jobs and nightly analytics runs.

Goals you articulated:
- Stable interactive latency target: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 110ms, p99 < 180ms for typical 512-token requests.
- Isolation: a single-tenant inference enclave (no shared tenant scheduling) with audit logs and KMS integration.
- Predictable monthly spend for budgeting/forecasting and a procurement-friendly contract term (12–24 months).
- Ability to scale burst capacity during nightly scoring windows without manual provisioning.

Technical constraints / environment:
- Primary region: us-west-2. On-prem ingest to S3 with private VPC peering to Redwood private control plane.
- Models: quantized variants of a 70B decoder; KV cache usage expected for chat-heavy paths.
- Expected baseline load: ~200 steady QPS (short sequences), bursts up to ~800 QPS during nightly scoring windows (30–90 minute duration).

Preliminary proposed enclosure (high level):
- Isolation: single-tenant enclave (we map to a reserved set of instances/nodes dedicated to NovaMed).
- Baseline fleet: 4x A100-class inference nodes (80GB equiv) with autoscaling headroom to 10 nodes for burst (policy-based).
- SLO targets to align with your goals: 99.95% monthly uptime SLA; p99 tail latency target 180ms for 512-token median workload (we will produce a test harness to verify under your seq distribution).
- Cost levers: batching + KV caching + quantized model variant for production inference; Redwood Optimize will surface concrete token-cost impact once we ingest a sample trace.

Deliverables we committed to: 
1) SLO matrix (attached: SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx) showing proposed latency/availability tiers and associated credits.
2) Isolation architecture sketch (attached: isolation_arch_sketch.png) — how VPC peering, host assignment, and audit trails work.
3) SOC2 & compliance extract (attached: SOC2-extract.pdf) and a brief on KMS integration.
4) A short proof-of-inference (POI) test plan we can run with a 24–48 hour load window to validate latency at your seq distribution.

Immediate next steps / asks:
- Alex: confirm procurement contact and your preferred contract length (12 vs 24 mo) and any internal PO cadence.
- NovaMed: share a 48-hour sample production trace (anonymized) or 1,000 representative requests so we can size batching/kv cache.
- Redwood: Ben & I will prepare a refined SLO + commercial sketch and a DocuSign-ready term sheet for the comms team by EOD Friday.

If that all looks right, we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive next week with Priyom and your infra lead to go over the POI test plan and the VPC peering steps.

Thanks again — good momentum here.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
mobile: (415) 555-0148

Attachment stubs: SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), isolation_arch_sketch.png (PNG diagram), SOC2-extract.pdf (PDF)
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novamed.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.ai>
Date: 2026-07-09T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference enclave qualification — post-call recap

Sean — thanks for the thorough recap, this is very helpful. High level notes / answers inline: 

- Procurement contact: procurement@novamed.ai (cc'd). Preferred term: 12 months to start, option to extend at 12-month mark.
- We can provide a 48-hour anonymized trace; I will pull that today and aim to drop it in the shared Drive link you sent.
- On isolation: necessity is non-negotiable for regulatory reasons. We need host-level separation (no shared GPUs) and per-request audit logs retained 365 days. KMS must be key-managed by our team.
- SLA: 99.95% is acceptable; we'd like a clear remediation pathway and playbook in the contract for priority incident response.

Questions: 
1) For the burst-to-10-node plan, how long is the cold-start time for autoscale? We need to understand whether burst is instant or requires a warm pool.
2) Can you confirm the test harness will run within our VPC via an ephemeral test token so we don't have to expose traces externally?

I'll coordinate procurement to review the term sheet when you send it. Looking forward to the deep-dive — can we target Tue 7/13 10:00 PT for the tech session?

— Alex
Alex Morgan
CTO, NovaMed AI
T: +1 206 555 0123
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference enclave qualification — post-call recap (internal)

Quick internal note — Alex confirmed 12 months and strict isolation + 365d logs and KMS by customer. Priyom, please start drafting the POI plan with the following constraints:
- Warm pool strategy: keep 2 nodes warm (steady-state) to reduce cold-start; autoscale target latency to add nodes within 2–3 minutes using snapshot images.
- Batching policy: dynamic batching with cutoff 128 tokens; for nightly scoring we'll open a temporary large-batch path to maximize throughput.
- Telemetry: ensure per-request tracing and log retention policy maps to 365 days and we can export to their S3 archive.

I'll prepare the initial commercial sketch and term sheet for Sean to send today. Also follow-up: ask legal about incident response playbook language for priority incidents.

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment reference: SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (draft)
